analysis: Lane-B3 exploratory: per-system certification breakdown + homogeneity check
status: EXPLORATORY (existing generations, no new compute) — but it AMENDED the CP7b prereg before comparator numbers landed
concentration: 29 of 34 certified cases are cubic or tetragonal; coverage is exactly 0 for hexagonal and monoclinic

homogeneity.verdict: odds ratios are NOT homogeneous and REVERSE SIGN across systems; a common odds ratio is not a defensible summary

why_it_matters: CMH by system is MORE significant than CMH by confidence, but pooling is inadmissible here. Reporting only the pooled z would have been a real error. The CP7b prereg is amended to gate CMH behind a Breslow-Day homogeneity test and to pre-declare per-stratum reporting when homogeneity is rejected.
new_secondary_hypothesis: H-CERT-3: the per-system coverage profile is SIMILAR across certifying chains, i.e. concentration in high-symmetry systems is a property of the task's symmetry structure rather than of process training. Testable against the B3 / SFT-V1 comparator arms now generating.
mechanistic_reading: the chain certifies where the lattice metric alone is nearly decisive (cubic/tetragonal) and fails where it is not (monoclinic/triclinic) — consistent with CP2's fabrication diagnosis and CP0c's finding that the geometry step is responsive to the image without being informed by it

prediction_collapse.implication: B1 can only be certified on a system the chain EMITS, so certification coverage is bounded by the chain's PREDICTION SUPPORT rather than its competence. Zero coverage on hexagonal/monoclinic is explained: the chain never predicts them.
prediction_collapse.self_correction: an intermediate note said coverage 'tracks the chain's own per-system accuracy almost exactly'. That overstates Pearson r=+0.677 over 7 points, and trigonal contradicts it (accuracy 0.967, coverage 0.067). Coverage is driven by prediction support; accuracy correlates with it only because both are high on cubic/tetragonal.
prediction_collapse.revised_H_CERT_3: do B3 and SFT-V1 show the SAME collapse? If yes, the coverage ceiling is a property of the task and chain format, not process training, and must be stated with the claim. If V2b's support is BROADER, that is a genuine process-training benefit.
